briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Ann Arbor Welcomes Lume While D.C. and Lansing Both Trend Toward Relief
briefs.top: Michigan's cannabis map keeps expanding — Lume just opened in Ann Arbor and UP operators are finding workarounds to the wholesale tax — while both parties' gubernatorial nominees now back repeal. Nationally, Compass Pathways' psilocybin program is sprinting toward an FDA filing and the DEA has formally argued for Schedule III, with cannabis M&A hitting a new gear behind the shift.

local.text: Michigan-based Lume Cannabis Co. opened its new Ann Arbor location at 2247 W. Liberty Street with a three-day grand opening celebration, adding fresh retail footprint right in THE STICKY TRAP's backyard.

Not every operator is retreating from the 24% wholesale tax: Rize, which runs three Upper Michigan locations, has kept growing by negotiating cost-sharing deals with suppliers that split the tax burden instead of eating it alone — and a compliance manager there says retail prices have only nudged from about $10 to $12, meaning the pain isn't fully hitting shelves.

Tax relief now has bipartisan momentum heading into November: GOP nominee John James unveiled a 'Freedom Agenda' plank to cut the cannabis excise tax from 10% to 5% and roll back the wholesale levy, arguing it 'drives up prices, gives illegal operators a competitive edge,' while Democratic primary rival Chris Swanson had already vowed to repeal the wholesale tax outright.

The Michigan Cannabis Industry Association's original wholesale-tax lawsuit is now headed to trial this month, giving operators a real court date and a concrete shot at rolling back the levy rather than just political promises.

The hard numbers: the wholesale tax pulled in only about $37 million in Q2 2026 and $34 million in Q1 against a $105 million-per-quarter projection, and active retail licenses statewide slipped from 845 to 836 year-over-year — real headwinds, but ammunition fueling the repeal push from both the legislature (HB 6224) and the governor's race.

national.text: Compass Pathways is in full launch-prep mode: shares jumped 5% Tuesday after the company announced a U.S. doctor education campaign ahead of Psych Congress and confirmed its psilocybin depression treatment COMP360 remains on track for a Q4 2026 NDA filing, with a possible U.S. launch in the first half of 2027.

The FDA holds a landmark public hearing on the future therapeutic use of psychedelic drugs on September 14, following its finalized clinical-trial guidance covering psilocybin, LSD and MDMA — analysts say the combination signals 'a more supportive regulatory environment that could reduce regulatory risk for psychedelic drug developers.'

Federal rescheduling keeps advancing: the DEA formally argued in its final post-hearing brief that marijuana should move from Schedule I to Schedule III, telling the court cannabis no longer meets Schedule I's statutory criteria, with an administrative law judge's recommendation now the next milestone to watch.

M&A is accelerating on the back of rescheduling momentum: Trulieve completed its move to the NYSE after posting $271 million in Q2 revenue, while Vireo Growth reported revenue up 335% year-over-year and announced a wave of new deals — including FLUENT, C21 and a Planet 13 merger — expanding into a 15th state.

Not every rescheduling ripple is smooth: the DEA is now sending Colorado medical cannabis businesses a detailed 26-question compliance checklist for federal protections tied to the new Schedule III pathway — a sign the agency is standing up real infrastructure for operators to plug into, even if paperwork comes first.
